title: Kellton Tech Solutions Ltd - 519602 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Kellton Q2 FY27 revenue rose 6.5% YoY to Rs 321 crore, with PAT of Rs 23 crore and EBITDA margin of 12.1%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of about Rs 321 crore (6.5% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 39 crore, PAT of Rs 23 crore and EPS of 43 paise, with H1 revenue of Rs 637 crore (6.6% YoY). Six new client wins were announced across automotive finance, US healthcare claims, Saudi aviation, automotive logistics, agri-tech and hearing aids, plus several AI hackathon and award recognitions. The call was dominated by capital-raising questions: a board-approved FCCB of Rs 50 million is on hold, and a rights issue awaits exchange approval with promoter participation. Management tied the fundraise to debt repayment, acquisitions and buying IP. The call was disrupted by audio issues, and several questions came from individual shareholders.

segments.name: segments
segments.commentary: No separate business-segment revenue or margin split was disclosed on the call; the only operating breakdown was by client win and by vertical (automotive finance, US healthcare claims, Saudi aviation, automotive logistics, agri-tech, hearing aids). Management gave no segment-level numbers.

guidance_outlook: No revenue or margin guidance was given on the call.
Rights issue: board-approved; exchange approvals (NSE and BSE) pending; management expects news around end-November or early December 2026 and says promoters will participate.

FCCB: board and shareholder enabling resolution in place, but management said there are no current plans to issue it and it will not happen soon, with dilution to be avoided until prices and market conditions improve.
capex_capacity: Proceeds from the fundraise are intended to retire debt, fund targeted acquisitions, and invest in IP such as the Phoenix AI platform and AI frameworks.
No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Six client wins in Q2: a global automotive finance company (enterprise loan integration platform, a base for AI credit decisioning); a US healthcare claims processor (AI-driven enterprise management platform); a Saudi low-cost airline (on-site quality engineering pods); a premium automotive logistics provider (IT infrastructure support after an initial audit); a seed engineering spin-off (four or five applications); and a top-five global hearing aid maker (software and firmware engineering and R&D in India).
Management said products attract higher valuation multiples than services and that IP-led revenue would scale at near-zero incremental cost per copy.

Niyama, an AI regulatory-compliance agent built for a SEBI tech sprint at the Global FinTech Fest, won first prize from 525 participants (25 finalists). It has drawn inbound interest from BFSI and FinTech customers.
Recognition: an ADB Emerging Excellence Award, with ADB now asking for help on a new Spain setup. SBI AURA hackathon placed fourth, for an agentic AI personalised-banking solution.

qa_highlights.question: How much dilution should shareholders expect from the Rs 50 million HCCB approved by the board in September?
qa_highlights.answer: The HCCB is on hold due to macro conditions. Management will dilute only when market and financial conditions improve and not at current prices, and the Rs 50 million raise is for debt repayment, acquisitions and IP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the rights issue approved by the board, and will promoters take part?
qa_highlights.answer: Applications have been filed with NSE and BSE and approvals are pending. Promoters will participate, and management expects news around end-November or early December.

qa_highlights.question: Why did goodwill rise significantly over the last year?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise came from a commodity acquisition. All overseas goodwill was written off, while Indian goodwill is retained because of Indian tax rules and will eventually need to be written off.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FCCB and rights issue together cause significant equity dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision has been taken. The rights issue should not dilute holders, since they can take up their proportionate shares. The FCCB would dilute, but there are no current plans for it and it will wait for better conditions.

risks_watch: Equity dilution from the rights issue and any future FCCB; the company says the stock price is currently too low to issue.
Debt on the books: management wants to retire debt, and the fundraise is partly for that purpose. No debt figures were disclosed.
Goodwill: Indian goodwill is still on the books and will eventually have to be written off; the amount was not quantified.
Execution of the IP and acquisition strategy, which depends on the fundraise and is not yet funded.
Macro and IT-sector valuation headwinds, which management cited as reasons for deferring the FCCB.
Exchange approval timing for the rights issue (management target is end-November or early December 2026).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term IP and AI positioning and on the bottom in the share price, but cautious and deferential on capital raising, deferring the FCCB and avoiding dilution at current prices. The call was disrupted by a dropped landline; some answers were repeated and clarity was limited. Management offered no hard numbers on debt, goodwill, or acquisition pipeline.
key_quotes: And we are not going to dilute at this price point because we believe that there is a lot more value in our stock than what is reflected currently.
So the 50 million that we are going to raise is to retire debt.
From a rights issue point of view, there should not be any dilution because whatever it is that you hold currently, you can get the same number of shares from the rights issue.
